primary_source.citation: Cossard GG & Pannell JR (2021). Enhanced leaky sex expression in response to pollen limitation in the dioecious plant Mercurialis annua. Journal of Evolutionary Biology 34:416–422
primary_source.status: Original publisher full text accessible and Methods, Results, Discussion verified; original individual Dryad CSV not fetched or refit

plant.mechanism: Female plants can produce rare staminate flowers (leaky sex expression); they may be located in leaf axils around pistillate flowers, not the normal male's stalked inflorescences
plant.unknown_inherited_reactivation: Phenotype plasticity is NOT molecular restoration after genetic loss

design.randomized_assignment_and_seed_pool: Seedlings raised 6 weeks in common greenhouse from mixed same seed pool, then effectively randomly assigned to field plots; individual genotypes not matched or cloned across treatments
design.pot_structure: 60 pots per plot ×3 plants, 3 plots per treatment; controls alternated 2M1F and 1M2F; all-female 3F per pot
design.male_reproductive_effort_definition: dry biomass of staminate male flowers / aboveground vegetative biomass of female plant
design.female_reproductive_effort_definition: dry biomass of female flowers and fruits/seeds / aboveground vegetative biomass of female plant
design.leakiness_threshold_rule: MRE greater than control-population female 95th percentile; 5% of controls classified leaky BY DEFINITION
design.alternative_threshold_robustness: Authors also analyzed any male flower and an 80th-percentile cutoff; qualitative findings similar

female_count_change_under_fixed_total_pl.causal_scope: Treatment replaces male plants by female plants; it manipulates mate/sex community at fixed total plant density, NOT pollen availability alone at constant female neighbour density

published_results.original_comparison_outcome: The MRE per female plant's aboveground vegetation is more than doubled in all-female plots; change in fraction of plants deemed leaky not significant
published_results.source_figure1_caption: Three all-female (S1-S3) and three 1:1 control (C1-C3) populations, with mean and SE for incidence, MRE and FRE

discussion.proposed_cue: Plants may sense reproductive pollen receipt or later fruit filling; neighbour sex recognition not demonstrated, and pot-level number of males had no detected effect
discussion.source_falsifiable_adaptive_plasticity_r: Demonstrate leaky plants reproduce more without mates AND nonleaky plants reproduce more when mates available in appropriate common genetics
discussion.island_colonization: Proposed as a plausible function of sex leakiness during mate-limited founder events; NO oceanic island plant population studied here
discussion.biogeography: Expansion-front metapopulations in western Europe can encounter mate-limited colonization and fluctuating density, but experiment in Swiss common gardens with Spanish-origin genotypes
discussion.context_with_2024_hexaploid: 2024 hexaploid M. annua male-sterile females often make visually male-like flowers without functional pollen; 2021 diploid XX females reactivate morphologically male flowers. These are biologically distinct cytotypes and studies.

limitations: The 2.33× effect is male-flower dry biomass per vegetative biomass, not count of male flowers, viability of pollen, number of mating partners or genetically confirmed selfed offspring
No same-clone repeated genotype across control and male-free treatment; plants from same mixed pool assigned to different environments on average
There are SIX plot-level replicate experimental populations (three each), 272 female plants nested among them and pots; do not treat 272 as independent population replicates
By construction 5% of control plants exceed control-based 95th percentile; incidence direction is non-significant p=.058 even though MRE mean response p=.01
Female reproductive effort difference p=.19 non-significant, which does NOT demonstrate zero cost of opposite-sex male flowers
No male flower pollen viability or source-verified actual offspring selfing rates from this 2021 manipulation
No experiment tested pollen addition independently of male absence, direct sensing cues unverified
2021 original dryad dataset is registered but CSV/text could not be fetched via available tools; no raw individual model refit here
Do not equate 2021 diploid XX female plastic male expression with 2024 hexaploid CMS female retained sterile male flowers, or combine their model coefficients
This plastic response supports preserved developmental ability, not evolutionary restoration of a genetically deleted male function
No allelic rare-type invasion, realized lifetime fitness, SLK Phi/g0/Delta_R, or historical origin directly observed

The all-female treatment doubles the number of females per equal-180-plant population (90 controls vs 180); mate absence is confounded with increased female-neighbour density/competition, and is NOT pure pollen supplementation or direct pollen signal intervention.
